in_hebrew.name: שבטינו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word 'shavat' (save) and 'yonah' (God), meaning 'God is our savior' or 'God saves us'. However, this name does not appear in the Hebrew Bible.

in_greek.name: Σεβαστιανός
in_greek.meaning: venerable, revered, or of the emperor
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek word 'sebastos' (venerable, revered, or of the emperor), which was a title given to the Roman emperor, and later adopted by Christians as a surname or given name. In the New Testament, the name 'Sebastian' appears in the Acts of the Apostles (8:37) and in Revelation (1:13) as a name given to seven angels.

in_latin.name: Sebastianus
in_latin.meaning: venerable, revered, or of the emperor
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'Sebastianus', which is derived from the Greek word 'sebastos' (venerable, revered, or of the emperor), and was a surname or given name used in the Roman Empire. In the Latin Vulgate Bible, the name 'Sebastian' appears in the Acts of the Apostles (8:37) and in Revelation (1:13).
